site.name: Byte Runner
site.tagline: Follow the bites. Eat the page.
site.description: A round, hungry pixel frog races through magnetic food pipes in the page’s whitespace. Jump out to eat real text, then catch another trail and hunt escaping flies.
site.versionNote: Food trails. Tiny feet. A very real page.
controls: Arrows / WASD / touch joystick — race through pipes and queue turns
Space / Jump button or double-tap a direction — jump out; touch a trail to reattach
M / Refresh maze — redraw trails · P — pause · G — next area · Esc — Recall
Scoreboard: sound · pause / resume · minimize · Recall

chapters.title: The UI is the terrain.
chapters.body: Soft maze edges trace the whitespace around text, controls and media. The frog sticks firmly to the centerline, carries speed through bends, and queues turns at junctions. Press Space or double-tap a direction to jump out anywhere. Eat real letters on your detours, then catch another trail.

chapters.title: Big glow. Bigger appetite.
chapters.body: Pink power squares emit a pulse and turn flies blue for six seconds, stacking up to nine. A quick red tongue grabs vulnerable flies up to two pellets ahead. Hunt them for 100, 200, 300, then 400 points. Fruit is optional bonus food.

chapters.title: Small feet. Big appetite.
chapters.body: Tiny ball-shaped feet scramble only while moving. Violet flies pursue directly, pink flies anticipate your heading, and cyan Roamers mix pursuit with wandering. Flies occasionally escape between pipes, but stay inside the visible playfield.

chapters.title: The DOM carries the trails.
chapters.body: Pellets twinkle independently and eaten squares leave a faint grey trail. Food returns on the simulation clock using the same SVG nodes. Pipes stay stable during play: scrolling, resizing, a new wave, or Refresh maze redraws them. Native scrolling carries everything with the page; real text stays mutated until Recall.

site.extra: Three lives. Eat every square once to clear a level. Up to five flies arrive immediately, building toward nine on the first level and twelve later where space permits. Recall removes game-owned creatures, food, and text edits.

characters.name: Byte Runner
characters.rules: A round green frog with a wide side chomp, expressive eyes and tiny ball-shaped feet. Nearby trails gently guide parallel movement; steer across them to roam freely and eat real letters.

characters.name: Chaser
characters.rules: The violet fly takes a corridor route toward your position. Unpowered contact costs a life.

characters.name: Interceptor
characters.rules: The pink fly aims several junctions ahead of your heading. Turn to change its interception point.

characters.name: Roamer
characters.rules: The cyan fly mixes fast pursuit with roaming at junctions. Its wings stay within the corridor routes.

characters.name: Vulnerable flies
characters.rules: A glowing power pellet seals the gates temporarily. Blue flies flee along the maze and become edible. Chain catches for increasing points.

characters.name: Power pellet
characters.rules: Large glowing pink squares give six seconds of power, capped at nine when stacked. Six to eight are spread along the trails; eaten power squares return after 20 seconds as bonus food.

characters.name: Bonus fruit
characters.rules: Cherries and strawberries appear on the corridors. Catch them before they disappear; they are optional bonus food.

page.lead: A round, hungry pixel frog races through food pipes drawn in this page's whitespace. Jump out to eat real text, grab glowing power and turn the tables on the flies. It plays right here in your browser: no install, and Recall gives the page back.
page.support: Play it here, then make it part of your own project. Visit GitHub for the source code, setup instructions, and integration examples.

howToPlay.title: Press Play
howToPlay.body: Food trails appear in the page's whitespace and gutters, with small pixel squares, larger glowing power squares and fruit.

howToPlay.title: Race the pipes
howToPlay.body: Arrows or WASD steer. The frog sticks to the pipe, queues your next turn and carries its speed around bends. On a phone, the joystick steers.

howToPlay.title: Jump out to eat text
howToPlay.body: Space, the Jump button or a quick double-tap releases the frog anywhere. Eat real page letters, then touch another trail to reattach.

howToPlay.title: Power up and hunt
howToPlay.body: Glowing power makes flies edible for six seconds, stacking to nine. The red tongue catches a vulnerable fly up to 54 pixels ahead.

howToPlay.title: Clear the level
howToPlay.body: Eat every small and glowing square once to clear a level, for a 500 × level bonus. You have three lives.

tips.title: Food grows back
tips.body: Eaten food returns after 12 seconds (20 for power) and scores again without resetting level progress. Real letters do not come back.

tips.title: Fruit is a bonus
tips.body: Fruit is optional bonus food, not a power-up.

tips.title: Redraw the maze
tips.body: M or Refresh maze rebuilds the trails from the page's layout.

tips.title: Expect company
tips.body: Up to five flies arrive at once, building toward nine on the first level and twelve later where space permits. G travels to the next area.

items.title: No zoom mid-run
items.body: While a run is live, a pinch, an iOS gesture or a double tap no longer zooms the page out of shape. One finger still plays and drags the scoreboard; the end of the run gives the zoom back.

items.title: The scoreboard still drags
items.body: Grab it with one finger on a phone or with the mouse; the drag never zooms the page.

items.title: On Fizlet 0.20.0
items.body: Same game and rules as before; the engine underneath is the only change to Byte Runner.

faq.q: Do I need to install anything to play Byte Runner?
faq.a: No. Byte Runner plays on this page in your browser. Press Play, and press Escape or Recall when you are done to give the page back.

faq.q: Can I play Byte Runner on a phone?
faq.a: Yes. A joystick steers the frog and a Jump button releases it from the trail.

faq.q: What happens to the page when I play?
faq.a: The frog eats real page letters, and its trails, food and creatures are drawn inside the page. Recall removes them and restores the text edits the game still owns.

faq.q: Can I put Byte Runner on my own site?
faq.a: Yes. It is open source (MIT). The GitHub repository has the source code, setup instructions and integration examples.
